statement: In an n-dimensional projective space, homogeneous coordinates are an (n+1)-tuple of coordinates (x_1, ..., x_{n+1}), not all zero, representing an equivalence class in R^{n+1} \ {0} under the equivalence relation (x_1, ..., x_{n+1}) ~ (lambda * x_1, ..., lambda * x_{n+1}) for any non-zero scalar lambda. For the projective plane (n = 2), a point is represented by a non-zero triple (X, Y, Z); when Z != 0, it corresponds to the Euclidean plane point (X/Z, Y/Z), and when Z = 0, it represents a point at infinity.

symbols.meaning: homogeneous coordinates of a point in the projective plane
homogeneous coordinates of a point in n-dimensional projective space
Cartesian coordinates of a point in the Euclidean plane when Z != 0
non-zero scalar factor relating equivalent representations
homogeneous line coordinates in the projective plane

properties.property: Scale equivalence: Two sets of homogeneous coordinates represent the same projective point if and only if one is obtained from the other by multiplying all coordinates by the same non-zero scalar lambda.
properties.why: Points in projective space are defined as equivalence classes of non-zero coordinate tuples under scalar scaling.

properties.property: Euclidean correspondence: When Z != 0, the homogeneous triple (X, Y, Z) corresponds to the Cartesian coordinates (X/Z, Y/Z) in the Euclidean plane, with the Euclidean origin given by (0, 0, 1).
properties.why: Dividing each coordinate by Z normalizes the representative to (X/Z, Y/Z, 1).

properties.property: Representation of points at infinity: When Z = 0, the triple (X, Y, 0) represents a point at infinity corresponding to the direction of a parallel family of lines.
properties.why: Taking the limit as the distance t along the line nx + my = 0 approaches infinity makes Z = 1/t approach 0, yielding direction coordinates (m, -n, 0).

properties.property: Dimension extension: An n-dimensional projective space requires (n + 1) homogeneous coordinates.
properties.why: One additional coordinate is required to allow the finite representation of points at infinity.

properties.property: Linear transformation representation: A change of coordinate system or projective transformation is represented by matrix multiplication (X, Y, Z)^T = A (x, y, z)^T for an invertible (n+1) x (n+1) matrix A.
properties.why: Invertible matrix multiplication preserves non-zeroness and commutes with non-zero scalar multiplication.

properties.property: Well-defined curve conditions: A condition f(x, y, z) = 0 is well-defined on projective points if and only if f is a homogeneous polynomial satisfying f(lambda*x, lambda*y, lambda*z) = lambda^k * f(x, y, z).
properties.why: Homogeneity ensures that f(x, y, z) = 0 if and only if f(lambda*x, lambda*y, lambda*z) = 0 for every non-zero lambda.

properties.property: Projective duality: A line sx + ty + uz = 0 can be represented by homogeneous line coordinates (s, t, u), which share identical algebraic and logical properties with point coordinates.
properties.why: The incidence relation sx + ty + uz = 0 is symmetric in the point coordinates (x, y, z) and line coordinates (s, t, u).

assumptions.assumption: The coordinate tuple cannot be all zeros; (0, ..., 0) is excluded.
assumptions.breaks_when: All coordinates evaluate to 0, which does not belong to R^{n+1} \ {0} and represents no point in projective space.

assumptions.assumption: The scaling constant lambda relating equivalent coordinates must be non-zero.
assumptions.breaks_when: lambda = 0, which collapses valid coordinates to the excluded all-zero tuple.

assumptions.assumption: Coordinates are drawn from a field (e.g., R, C) or a division ring where multiplication order is respected.
assumptions.breaks_when: The underlying ring contains zero divisors or non-commutative multiplication without specifying left/right action.

failure_modes.cause: Attempting to assign all zeros or multiplying coordinates by scalar lambda = 0.
Attempting to map a point at infinity (where Z = 0) directly into finite Euclidean Cartesian coordinates.

failure_modes.signature: Truth value of f(x, y, z) = 0 depends on the specific choice of representative coordinates
failure_modes.cause: Evaluating an inhomogeneous function where f(lambda*x, lambda*y, lambda*z) != lambda^k * f(x, y, z), making the zero set ill-defined on equivalence classes.
